title: Lift a field-groupoid point with both residue-field maps invertible
statement: Let $k$ be a field [def-weil-field], $V=\operatorname{Spec}k$ [def-weil-affine-spectrum], and $(V,R,s,t,e,i,c)$ an absolute groupoid scheme [def-a1-groupoid-scheme]. For every point $r\in|R|$ there exist a field extension $K/k$ [def-pc-field-extension] with $K$ algebraically closed (every nonconstant polynomial over $K$ has a root in $K$), and a point $r_K\in|R_K|$, where $R_K=\operatorname{Spec}K\times_{V,t}R\times_{s,V}\operatorname{Spec}K$ [def-pc-fibre-product], with its induced groupoid operations, such that the middle projection $p:R_K\to R$ sends $r_K$ to $r$ and both source and target induce field isomorphisms $K\to\kappa(r_K)$ [def-weil-residue-field]. No finite-type or perfectness assumption on $k$ or $R$ is imposed.

proof.text: Put $E=\kappa(r)$ and write $a=s^*:k\hookrightarrow E$, $b=t^*:k\hookrightarrow E$ for the residue-field embeddings [def-weil-residue-field]. Apply [lem-sfb-large-algclosed-field-extension] to $E$ to choose an embedding $\sigma:E\hookrightarrow K$ into an algebraically closed field with $\max(\aleph_0,|E|)<\operatorname{trdeg}_P K$. Define $\iota=\sigma a$ and give $K$ its $k$-extension structure through $\iota$.

source.place: Tag 04LR (lemma-groupoid-on-field-explain-points), proof, constructions (1)-(2): choose the overfield and its residue-field embedding.

proof.text: The two embeddings $\iota,\sigma b:k\hookrightarrow K$ need not agree. Since $a:k\hookrightarrow E$ is injective, $|k|\leq |E|$, whence $\max(\aleph_0,|k|)<\operatorname{trdeg}_P K$. Therefore [lem-sfb-small-field-embeddings-conjugate], applied with $F=k$ and these two prescribed embeddings, supplies an automorphism $\tau:K\xrightarrow{\sim}K$ satisfying $\tau\iota=\sigma b$. This gives the precise commuting field diagram needed for the two changed object factors.

source.place: Tag 04LR (lemma-groupoid-on-field-explain-points), proof, construction (3): conjugate the two k-embeddings.

proof.text: Let $j_r:\operatorname{Spec}E\to R$ be the canonical point morphism and put $h=j_r\circ\operatorname{Spec}\sigma$. The field-point bijection [lem-weil-pbc-morphism-from-spec-field] gives image $r$. Naturality [lem-weil-pbc-residue-field-point-naturality], and contravariant functoriality of Spec [def-weil-affine-spectrum], give $sh=\operatorname{Spec}(\sigma a)=\operatorname{Spec}\iota$ and $th=\operatorname{Spec}(\sigma b)=\operatorname{Spec}\iota\circ\operatorname{Spec}\tau$. Thus the triple $(\operatorname{Spec}\tau,h,\mathrm{id}_{\operatorname{Spec}K})$ defines $f:\operatorname{Spec}K\to\operatorname{Spec}K\times_{V,t}R\times_{s,V}\operatorname{Spec}K=R_K$ by the two fibre-product universal properties [def-pc-fibre-product]. It satisfies $pf=h$, $s_Kf=\mathrm{id}$ and $t_Kf=\operatorname{Spec}\tau$.

source.place: Tag 04LR (lemma-groupoid-on-field-explain-points), proof, translation of the displayed field diagram into the restricted groupoid.

proof.text: Let $r_K$ be the image of the unique point under $f$. Then $p(r_K)=r$. Write $\rho:\kappa(r_K)\hookrightarrow K$ for its field-point map [lem-weil-pbc-morphism-from-spec-field], and $\alpha_s,\alpha_t:K\to\kappa(r_K)$ for the residue maps of the two projections. Apply residue-field naturality to these projections and compare the factorizations of $s_Kf$ and $t_Kf$ through their canonical point morphisms. Uniqueness in the field-point bijection gives $\rho\alpha_s=\mathrm{id}_K$ and $\rho\alpha_t=\tau$, using the residue-field identification of the one-point scheme $\operatorname{Spec}K$ [def-weil-affine-spectrum]. Since $\rho$ is injective, the first equality also implies $\alpha_s\rho=\mathrm{id}_{\kappa(r_K)}$. Hence $\alpha_s=\rho^{-1}$ and $\alpha_t=\rho^{-1}\tau$ are both isomorphisms.

source.place: Tag 04LR (lemma-groupoid-on-field-explain-points), proof, verification of both residue-field isomorphisms from the field diagram.

proof.text: The restricted groupoid operations are induced by the original ones. Explicitly, an $H$-point is a triple $(u_t,g,u_s)$ with $t(g)=q\circ u_t$ and $s(g)=q\circ u_s$, where $q=\operatorname{Spec}\iota$. Its identity, inverse, and composition are $(u,e(qu),u)$, $(u_s,i(g),u_t)$, and $(u_2,c(g_2,g_1),u_0)$ on composable triples $(u_2,g_2,u_1),(u_1,g_1,u_0)$. These define scheme morphisms by [def-pc-fibre-product]; their laws follow componentwise from [def-a1-groupoid-scheme]. Thus the operations required in the statement exist, and the field and point above have all the asserted properties.

source.place: Tag 04LR (lemma-groupoid-on-field-explain-points), statement: restriction of the groupoid; its operations by the fibre-product universal property.
